newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa soars to two-month highs on Ivory news.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa soars to two-month highs on Ivory news.

text.p: CSCE cocoa prices shot up to their highest level in two months on Friday, bolstered by heavy speculative short-covering amid the prospect of a smaller Ivorian harvest, trading sources said.

Most-active May futures surged $67 a tonne -- or five percent -- on the day, to close at $1,392, having traded from $1,395 to $1,341. July finished $65 higher, at $1,413, while the rest rose $43 to $65.
Prices gapped some $20 higher at the outset on the heels of a strong showing in London, traders said. London's key May contract ended up 35 stg, to 981 stg.
"New York was fueled by London's strength, which took us through some stops," said Refco Inc. analyst Ann Prendergast, "and the perception of smaller West African crops."

At the International Cocoa Organization meeting in London Monday, Ivorian Commodities Minister Alain Gauze reaffirmed the country's 1996/97 cocoa crop will be below one million tonnes. He added that the Ivory Coast has already sold around 800,000 tonnes but has no more cocoa to sell.

Private estimates for top-producer Ivory Coast's 1996/97 cocoa crop have been as high as 1.1 million tonnes while the government's official crop forecast, including mid-crop, published in December was 950,000 tonnes.
Additionally, Gauze said the Ivory Coast's planned to destroy all cocoa and coffee planted illegally in national forests, which amounted to about 100,000 tonnes of cocoa and coffee last year.
"Fundamentally, production will be smaller this year and stocks will decline," said Smith Barney analyst Walt Spilka. "There will be no shortage but there will be less cocoa available this year."
Spilka noted that cocoa prices were still relatively cheap compared with their 20-year price average of $1,900. He said prices were likely to peak at around $1,700 to $1,800 this year.
While traders said speculative short-covering accounted for the majority of the day's gains, they noted some arbitrage interest and a smattering of outright speculative buying.
"I think this may be the tip of the iceberg of new buying coming in," one trader said. "But the key is London."

New York traders are expecting London to open 15-20 stg higher Tuesday, he said, adding that if London makes its due New York would have little trouble breaching key psychological resistance $1,400 basis March. On the downside, the market is likely to react negatively to a break below $1,360.
An estimated 22,758 lots changed hands on the day, nearly double Friday's official total of 10,842.
